title: Form Lookups Demo
---

# Lookups in Inputs and Template forms

An `<Inputs>` or `<Template>` block's `boilerplate.yml` can declare lookups with `x-` keys, the same ones a `<TfModule>` module's `runbook_block.yml` declares without the prefix. A lookup asks an API for rows, through the auth block the form's `auth` prop binds its group to, and a field uses them:

- `x-lookup` suggests values as you type.
- `x-prefill` fills an empty field when the lookup finds exactly one row.
- `x-shortcut` adds a button that sets the field from the lookup's one row.

This runbook's lookups are in `_includes/google.yml`, which both forms include with `x-include`. Until someone signs in below, the fields say so, and take typed values.

## Sign in to Google Workspace

<GoogleAuth
  id="workspace"
  scopes={[
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email",
    "openid",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly",
  ]}
/>

## An Inputs block

The YAML is written in the runbook, so `x-include` is relative to the runbook.

<Inputs id="owner" auth={{ google: "workspace" }}>
```yaml
x-include:
  - _includes/google.yml
variables:
  - name: Owner
    type: string
    description: Who owns the team's resources. Filled with you once you sign in.
    x-prefill: { from: google.me }
  - name: Reviewers
    type: list
    description: Who reviews changes
    x-lookup: { from: google.people }
```
</Inputs>

## A Template block

The template's `boilerplate.yml` includes the same file, relative to itself.

<Template id="team" path="templates/team" auth={{ google: "workspace" }} />
